title: How Curse grew from a WoW add-on site to 23M monthly visitors
summary: Hubert Thieblot explains how Curse grew from a guild add-on tool he built alone into a 64-site gaming network. He covers hiring real gamers, using pro players as content producers, expanding across games, and monetizing via ads when costs outgrew his means.

principles.text: Start by solving your own community's problem; a useful internal tool can become a product for others.
principles.quote: The Website ended up being a useful tool, not just for members of the guild, but for other players as well.

principles.text: Hire true users of your product; their feedback is the best product signal.
principles.quote: When we are seeking new employees, it’s very important for us to hire real gamers.

principles.text: If your own staff uses your products, you will end up making good products.
principles.quote: If our staff uses our products, then we will make good products

principles.text: Expand beyond a niche once the market is too small: add new games, tools, and content types.
principles.quote: When we moved to the U.S., the market was too niche and we decided to grow and expand our offerings.

principles.text: When costs outgrow what you can cover, add ads as a revenue model to pay the bills.
principles.quote: My oldest brother suggested that ads could be a possible solution to generate profit and pay the bills.

principles.text: Use real experts as content contributors, not just as a branding play.
principles.quote: Real pro gamers are the best content contributors to create new guides.
